item.title: JJ Redick goes off on the Lakers' bench after almost blowing the lead against the Raptors
item.description: JJ Redick goes off on the Lakers' bench after almost blowing the lead against the Raptors originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Los Angeles Lakers had one of their best performances of their 2026-27 season so far against the Toronto Raptors. They went up by as much as 26 points and led by 16 points in the final two minutes of the game. This prompted Lakers head coach JJ Redick to clear out his bench to see out the game. Unfortunately, the bench unit did not live up to expectations, as they almost blew the lead. This led to Redick sending Luka Doncic, Austin Reaves, Walker Kessler, and Matisse Thybulle back in to see out the game and get the 131-125 win. JJ Redick admits he is disappointed by the Lakers' bench after almost blowing the game It is normal for coaches to send in their bench players to see out a game, especially when they have a lead as big as 16 points. However, what the Lakers' bench players showed against the Raptors was a bad sign, which is why Redick is putting his foot down. He does not like what happened in the game against the Raptors, especially since he wanted to rest his starters. Unfortunately for the Lakers, Redick had to send the starters back in because he wanted to secure the win rather than give up the massive lead in just a couple of minutes. MORE: JJ Redick speaks on what it's like seeing Luka Doncic dominate up close Thankfully for Redick and the Lakers, the starters were stable enough to get the result. It was a big win for the Lakers, but it does show some bad signs if the mediocre bench performances continue, which could have a long-term effect on the players and the coaching staff's approach to games. "I won’t make that mistake again. I’ll leave the guys in. You got to play to the final buzzer," Redick said about sending his bench in after getting a 16-point lead . It will be a big lesson for the Lakers moving forward, not only for Redick, but also for the players. When they are playing with a massive lead late into the game, the players must learn how to deal with the pressure and close out the win. It should never be stepping off the gas, they just need to balance their aggression with some semblance of control to get the win without any issue. item.title: How will Wales fare on Nations Championship return?
item.description: Wales have won three Tests under head coach Steve Tandy [Huw Evans Picture Agency] Wales will start their international season next weekend when they return to the Nations Championship. Steve Tandy's side face four games as they host Japan, New Zealand and Australia in Cardiff, before a final play-off match at the Allianz Stadium completes the November schedule. The autumn games begin the road to the 2027 World Cup in Australia in a year's time. BBC Sport Wales provides a recap of what has happened so far in the inaugural running of the global tournament and looks at what lies in wait over the next month. What is the Nations Championship? The Nations Championship pits the northern hemisphere teams who compete in the Six Nations - England, Ireland, Scotland, Wales, France and Italy - against southern hemisphere giants South Africa, New Zealand, Australia and Argentina, plus invited sides Fiji and Japan. All teams play each of the six nations in the opposing hemisphere once, with three rounds of fixtures having already been staged in July and now another three in November. Their results will rank the teams within their own hemisphere, from one to six, before a final play-off weekend at the Allianz Stadium in Twickenham. Where are Wales internationals really made? Wales counting down the year until World Cup How have Wales fared so far and who do they play next? Wales will resume the Nations Championship in fifth place in the northern hemisphere standings after a mixed July campaign. It started with an encouraging six-try victory against Fiji at the Cardiff City Stadium, which was considered a home venue for the Pacific Islanders side. But Wales faltered during a demanding travelling schedule as they were outclassed by Argentina in San Juan and thrashed by South Africa in Durban. Now they face a trio of home games in Cardiff with the opening match staged against Eddie Jones' Japan side, who also sit fifth in their table, with the two teams potentially meeting twice this November. The tests will become harder when Dave Rennie brings his New Zealand side to Cardiff on 14 November, before the Wallabies arrive seven days later. Apathy has arrived on November 1st after the Eagles lost their sixth-straight game, stumbling against the previously one-win Washington Commanders, 27-10, at Northwest Stadium on Sunday night. The last time the Eagles lost six-straight games was in 2012, Andy Reid’s last season that ended in a 4-12 finish. Right now, the Eagles, who are 2-6, can only wish that they might win four games this season. It’s where teams that give up go. Yes, the Eagles are that bad (but lately can be used as a great sedative) . Here, it said the Eagles season was through after the 25-14 loss to Carolina in Week 6. Many believe that sentiment now. The Eagles are in sole possession of last place in the NFC East at 2-6, behind 2-4-1 Washington, 3-5 Dallas and the 4-2-1 New York Giants. After Rachaad White’s clinching touchdown with 1:52 left to play, chants of “Eagles suck, Eagles suck,” were heard throughout Northwest Stadium. Who could argue? The Eagles played as complete a game as a lowly, lifeless, capitulating team can. They were awful in all three phases: special teams, defense and offense. In the second half, the Eagles averaged an NFL-low 5.3 yards and 111 yards of offense entering the game managed to even sink below that against Washington, getting shutout in the second half and gaining 155 yards, blown up by cosmetic plays in the last minute. item.title: Wolff hits back at critics after title win: "This is Kimi Antonelli!"
item.description: Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff could not hide his satisfaction with Kimi Antonelli 's historic title win at the Mexico City GP, yet again pointing to the naysayers that claimed the Italian was too young for F1 . Antonelli's P3 finish at the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez, behind fellow champions Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton, respectively, was more than enough to secure a historic F1 Drivers' title. The 20-year-old has now beaten former Red Bull driver Sebastian Vettel’s age record - achieved at the Abu Dhabi GP in 2010 - by three years and 66 days to become F1’s youngest ever title winner. Speaking briefly to Sky Sports amidst the celebrations in Mexico City, Wolff said: "[People asked] Why do you put this kid in the car? Oh, it's Kimi Antonelli. THIS is Kimi Antonelli! Incredible. Also today, completely serene. That's what makes him so different." Wolff later appeared again with the broadcaster, going into further detail on why he was right to back the young Italian. “We have to pinch ourselves because it seems like yesterday he was 11 years old in a garage in junior karting and it goes so fast. “He wins the junior formulas, then a difficult year in F2 and that's already where people start outside started to doubt. Then when Lewis told me he was going to Ferrari, it was my immediate reaction that we’ve got to put him in the car." Wolff proud after Antonelli proves doubters wrong Photo: Race Pictures Photo: Race Pictures Wolff even revealed sponsors left Mercedes upon Antonelli's promotion but despite knowing the "calculated risk" of handing a then 18-year-old Antonelli his debut in 2025, the Austrian expressed his pride in backing the Italian. “But people doubted. We had two sponsors leaving us because of that, because of ‘who is this kid?’ There were others who stayed with us until today. Some are here that reaped the full reward. “And then the difficult year and people said again, he shouldn't even be in Formula 1 or he should be at a smaller team. Over nine races, no points, the tears in Spa and then this. “I'm just so proud for the team that all of them continue to trust him and he delivered. It was instinctive. Lewis left. I called Bradley and said, Kimi is in the car next year. We knew the data, so it kind of felt the right thing to do. I think it was always a calculated risk, not a real risk.”

item.description: Mauricio Pochettino’s U.S. roster announcement for the first official matches since the World Cup is days away, but beyond decisions common before every international window, he must also sort out whether his young prospects belong with the first team or the junior platoon with Olympic medal aspirations. Starting Nov. 9, the squads will gather separately — Pochettino’s for the CONCACAF Nations League’s quarterfinals against Haiti and Steve Cherundolo’s under-23s for a head start on the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. Had Pochettino not invited a dozen newcomers to senior camp six weeks ago, the intrigue this week wouldn’t rise above a typical selection. During victories over Peru, Chile, Mexico and Canada, however, several showed they were up to the challenge. In all likelihood, many will join Cherundolo for what is expected to be an overseas camp and friendlies. Cherundolo worked with Pochettino’s staff at the last camp, and the two coaches are collaborating on this week’s selections. With greater public attention on an Olympics at home, the U.S. Soccer Federation has placed extra emphasis on building a strong team. (Olympic men’s soccer is restricted to players 23 and under, with three overage exceptions.) Cherundolo will conduct additional camps in many of the international windows over the next 18 months. In a top-25 Big Ten conference matchup under the Friday night lights, Illinois quarterback Luke Altmyer and the Illini outplayed star Nebraska freshman quarterback Dylan Raiola and the Cornhuskers. It was a back-and-forth game all night. After a five-plus minute drive Nebraska — with its backup kicker in the game — would miss a 39-yard effort to set up a game-winning drive opportunity for Illinois. It ultimately led to overtime. Altmyer delivered in overtime as he threw a touchdown on the first drive to wide receiver Pat Bryant. The Illinois (4-0, 1-0 Big Ten) offense looked poised all night. Altmyer in particular had another impressive performance going 21-of-27, four touchdowns, and again zero interceptions. For most of the night, a poised Raiola led the way for Nebraska (3-1, 0-1 Big Ten), as he finished regulation with 284 yards and 3 touchdowns through the air. Illinois opened the game doing exactly what it needed to do if they wanted to win: set the tone with an opening drive touchdown. Halloween horror stories are nothing new, but this was an effort straight from the George A.Romero school of brutality and the latest horrific result to which Sunderland’s fans have been subjected. In classic splattercore fashion, the Lads ran straight towards the danger in the Midlands, looked entirely unprepared for what was coming, and were duly picked off. Nine points were on offer from our three most recent league outings, and we banked a total of one. Not good enough. Nowhere near. item.title: Sunderland Must Find Answers Fast – Or Face the Consequences
item.description: SUNDERLAND, ENGLAND - OCTOBER 25: Regis Le Bris, Manager of Sunderland portrait on the bench before during the Premier League 2026/27 match between Sunderland and Leeds United at Stadium of Light on October 25, 2026 in Sunderland, England. (Photo by Richard Sellers/Sportsphoto/Allstar via Getty Images) | Getty Images The message to the Sunderland squad is very clear: sort your shit out. Stop letting each other down. One fact remains for Régis Le Bris’ side that should offer some comfort: the team is playing so far within themselves that it almost defies belief. Where is what made them the group they were last season, and why has it disappeared? It is a club where various areas are letting themselves down when they don’t have to. Petulance, disconnect, tactical confusion, and meek surrender are the cornerstones of this football club right now – in the league, at least. A team that cannot defend and doesn’t take its chances. A team that is set up in a way that doesn’t have a proper shape or wingers. Brian Brobbey up front can look alarmingly isolated. Players whose body language has fluctuated between committed and disgracefully complacent. Did we not learn anything from last season? If not, then the lesson bears repeating: nothing comes easily in this division. It felt like we had to have the pedal pressed to the metal just to reach 40 points. It was hard. Very hard. Yes, there is the relative success in the cup competitions, but that feels very much like Alan Partridge’s still-good news about the chocolate oranges. It is not what he will be judged by. Of course, there are mitigating factors – injuries and the World Cup haven’t helped at all – but they will affect all sides in the Premier League. Sunderland are not unique in that regard. Can Le Bris survive? Given the fixtures coming up, it would seem unlikely, particularly alongside the track record of the board. Sadly, prior achievements rarely outweigh the urgent business of survival. Just ask Claudio Ranieri at Leicester a decade ago. If he does go, it would be devastating, because we have so much to thank him for. But given the possible repercussions of failing to make a change, it might be that his position is untenable, unless Sunderland get two victories in the next four games. The only thing which will save Le Bris is proving he has the answers. Yet that process should have begun against Coventry, but there was no response whatsoever. Brown walked out of Roker Park immediately after a meeting with Sunderland directors, including chairman Keith Collings, without saying goodbye to the players. But a day had gone by, and Brown was tracked down at his home by journalists and had given his reaction: I’ve been in this game much too long for anything to come as a surprise. I feel no bitterness towards anyone. In fact I shall continue to be a Sunderland supporter. I always have been, ever since I was a toddler. I shall go to watch them play whenever I can. I still believe that the club can be one of the forces in the game within five years. They have so many talented young players if only they are allowed time to develop. I shan’t have any personal contact with them now. Not that I don’t want to but I think it would be unfair to whoever takes over to interfere with him in any way. I still think I have a lot left to give the game. There’s no fitter man than me in the game today. There’s no rush but I’ll start looking around eventually. I have no desire to go round stabbing anyone in the back because of what has happened today. I don’t want to know what the directors have said in their statement. That is entirely a matter for them. My only immediate thought is that I am sorry to have to leave behind what I still consider to be a fine bunch of players. For what it is worth, I thought when I went to the ground today that it might be for the final time. But I really didn’t think about it a great deal. There were a lot of other things to be getting on with. I think you can safely say that my association with the club is over once and for all. If you look at my history you will see that I don’t go anywhere more than twice. That’s what my life is these days, I don’t know in what capacity. I have no thoughts about whether it will be another manager’s job or coaching or something else. I have nothing fixed up for the immediate future. The chairman had not made himself available for comment, but in a short statement, the club said: At a meeting this morning it was unanimously agreed that Mr. Alan Brown’s contract be terminated forthwith. No decision has been made as to his successor and this will be discussed at tomorrow’s board meeting. Brown’s contract was due to expire at the end of the season and were reported to be £250,000 in debt and losing £2,000 a week and the previous week, three new directors joined the Roker Park board, a move described by Mr. Collings as “the first stage in putting the club in order.” What’s Next? (Photo by Michael Steele/Getty Images) | Getty Images Well, I wrote my last editorial on 12th October, which you can read here , and I explained my worries about how things were going then. It’s now three weeks down the road, and we’re in big trouble. Bottom of the Premier League table after a quarter of the season has gone, four points behind Coventry in 16th, with only one side in the league having scored fewer goals (Forest in 19th) and only one having conceded more (Palace in 18th). Like I said, we’re right in the sh*t. Our last three games against Bournemouth, Leeds and Coventry were a chance to turn our season around – and we took one point from a possible nine. Looking at our next five league games, I just don’t know where the points will come from if the Sunderland from last season doesn’t turn up soon. For too many weeks now, we’ve been saying we expect a reaction in the next game, but time and again, it hasn’t happened. At some point, you simply run out of next games – one way or another. The reaction of the players and the manager after the goalless draw against Leeds was that we’d turned a corner, but that was all relative when compared to the dross served up in the majority of games in the Premier League so far. The way I see the season so far is that we turned up in the first half at Brentford, then at home to Arsenal and away at Pep-less City. And that’s it for me. item.title: NBA fans have mixed reactions to Scottie Barnes and Luka Doncic's scuffle during Lakers vs Raptors
item.description: Photo by Katelyn Mulcahy/Getty Images Luka Doncic and Scottie Barnes were involved in a little altercation during the Los Angeles Lakers’ win over the Toronto Raptors. The Lakers superstar dominated the game and led them to a very impressive 131-125 win in Los Angeles on Sunday night, but the Raptors did what they could to get under his skin. At one point in the game, Barnes and Doncic got into a scuffle, and that seems to have divided NBA fans over whose fault it actually was. NBA fans react to Luka Doncic and Scottie Barnes’ scuffle during Lakers vs Raptors At first glance, it looked like it was Barnes trying to tangle arms with Doncic, and many felt that the former should’ve been penalised for that. However, several others on the internet have pointed the finger at the Lakers star for his role in the scuffle. One fan tweeted: “How is that a double foul? Dude is trying to walk, and Scottie is wrapping his arm up.” Another wrote: “How do you call a foul on Luka there? “You can blatantly see Scottie tangling arms with Luka,” said another. One fan with an opposing stance said: “I hate when Luka does this. Man up and fight through the contact, man.” Another reacted by saying: “No way Luka is crying about this.” “This is what Yaxel was talking about. Watch Luka looking at the referee,” wrote another. Fans can pick sides between Barnes and Doncic all they like, but it’s the latter who had the last laugh with a fantastic performance. Doncic scored 45 points, while recording 15 rebounds, six assists and five steals. He was easily the best player on the court and was the reason why the Lakers won the game. The Lakers are now 5-2 this season, while the Raptors are stuck at 3-3. item.description: DENVER, CO - NOVEMBER 1: Head coach Sean Payton of the Denver Broncos looks at the scoreboard during the second quarter against the Kansas City Chiefs at Empower Field at Mile High on November 1, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) Getty The Denver Broncos may have just gotten what seemed like a breakout performance from rookie running back Jonah Coleman in a 28-24 win over the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 8 — but it’s important to remember that all of this is relative. According to DNVR’s Zac Stevens, the Broncos are still very much going after Indianapolis Colts running back and NFL All-Pro Jonathan Taylor, no matter how great Coleman looked on Sunday. “I believe the Broncos are going to do everything in their power to trade for Jonathan Taylor,” Stevens said on Sunday night. “This could happen at any moment. You might not want to go to sleep Broncos Country. The Broncos are going to try to pull this trade off, from my understanding. They want Jonathan Taylor now.” ESPN’s Adam Schefter and NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport previously named the Broncos as one of the teams circling a trade for Taylor. Schefter and Rapoport reported that the Broncos, Green Bay Packers , Seattle Seahawks , and Minnesota Vikings are chasing Taylor. The Athletic’s Jonathan Jones added the New York Giants to the list of “possible suitors.” “The Green Bay Packers, Seattle Seahawks, Denver Broncos and Vikings are among the teams that have pondered, or are expected to consider, the possibility of a trade for the star running back, according to sources,” Schefter and Rapoport wrote on October 25. The price for Taylor, reportedly, is similar to what the San Francisco 49ers gave up when they obtained running back Christian McCaffrey from the Carolina Panthers in 2022 — a 2nd, 3rd, 4th, and 5th-round pick. Jonathan Taylor: Elite RB on Terrible Team Taylor, 5-foot-10 and 226 pounds, has toiled as one of the NFL’s elite running backs on one of the league’s worst teams and worst-run franchises since the Colts drafted him in the 2nd round (No. 41 overall) of the 2020 NFL Draft after a record-setting career at Wisconsin. As a rookie, Taylor rushed for 1,169 yards and 11 touchdowns in 15 games before leading the NFL in rushing yards and touchdowns in 2021 with 1,851 yards and 18 touchdowns. After two injury-riddled seasons in 2022 and 2023, Taylor bounced back in a big way, rushing for 1,431 yards and 11 touchdowns in 2024 and 1,585 yards and 18 rushing touchdowns in 2025. item.title: Rams Head Coach Sean McVay Hilariously Says He Will ‘Crush’ Aaron Donald
item.description: Head coach Sean McVay accepted blame for the Los Angeles Rams losing to the San Francisco 49ers in Week 1. Getty The Los Angeles Rams scored a much-needed victory over the lowly Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday and head coach Sean McVay was in better spirits than he’s been for much of what has been a pretty disappointing season. He was able. to laugh and joke about his star defensive lineman Aaron Donald who made a pretty embarrassing blunder during the game. Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert lost control of the football as he was scrambling on one play deep in his own territory and Donald, the 35-year-old future Hall of Fame inductee, tried to track down the ball and would have had an easy scoop and score had he come up with it cleanly but he didn’t get a good grasp on it, kicked it a bit, and the ball ended up going out of bounds which meant that the Chargers retained possession of the ball when the Rams should have had prime field position at the very worst. McVay was asked about the play after the game and he said the following: “Aw man, I’m going to give him such a hard time about that. I mean, I saw what he was thinking because it’s going right in front of you and he’s thinking, ‘I’m going to scoop and score,’ and he knocks that [expletive] out of bounds, I mean, what the [expletive]. So, his face he couldn’t even look at me and make eye contact after that.” He also reportedly said, “I’m gonna crush him for that,” per J.B. Long. Rams could use some laughs amidst rough start to the season It was a much-needed win which brings the Rams to 4-4 on the season. Many analysts predicted they would be a superteam at the start of the season but perhaps those expectations were far too lofty as the team has looked rather pedestrian at best and just downright bad at certain times throughout the campaign so the fact they were able to take care of business against a bad opponent is good news for the Rams. An optimist would look at their situation and feel pretty good about things. Their next two games should be wins on paper as they will play the Washington Commanders and Arizona Cardinals, although they did lose to Arizona at home earlier this season, before their bye week in Week 11. They are still without Myles Garrett so if they can get him and some of their other injured players back for a late season run and are able to enter the playoffs with some momentum, even if they don’t end up winning the NFC West, then they will still be a team that no one in the NFC wants to face. That funny Donald moment may be a nice little bit of levity for McVay who can certainly run hot at times. There hasn’t been much to laugh about this season so moments like that matter just to ease the pressure a little bit. The Los Angeles Rams took care of business against the Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday, but Sean McVay and team president Kevin Demoff apparently have very different views on the crosstown matchup. After the Rams’ 24-9 win at SoFi Stadium , McVay was asked whether he considers the Chargers a rival. His answer was short and to the point. “Kevin Demoff does. I don’t,” McVay said, via Gary Klein of the Los Angeles Times. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Demoff, for his part, did not hide his excitement about the result. The Rams president celebrated on X with a GIF of Will Ferrell’s Ron Burgundy from “Anchorman” saying, “That’s amazing,” which ESPN’s Adam Schefter later shared. McVay’s comments are not surprising. The Rams and Chargers have both called Los Angeles home since relocating about a decade ago and now share SoFi Stadium, but they rarely see each other. The NFL schedule pairs the two teams only about once every four years, and Sunday’s game was just their second meeting since the stadium opened in 2020. Their facilities are also far apart, with the Rams practicing in the western San Fernando Valley and the Chargers based more than 30 miles away in El Segundo. McVay also made it clear before the game that he was not overlooking the winless Chargers. “I really couldn’t care less what the record says,” McVay said last week . “I see a team that’s really good. They led 9-3 behind three Cameron Dicker field goals before Kyren Williams punched in a 1-yard touchdown run late in the second quarter to give Los Angeles a 10-9 halftime lead. The Rams took over from there. Blake Corum broke free for a 23-yard touchdown run early in the third quarter, and Matthew Stafford found Puka Nacua for an 18-yard score to make it 24-9. The defense did the rest, intercepting the Chargers twice and recording two sacks while holding them scoreless after halftime. The win improved the Rams to 4-4 and gave them their second straight victory. The Chargers, meanwhile, remain winless . Whether McVay calls it a rivalry or not, the Rams now hold an 8-6 edge in the all-time series. They will visit the Washington Commanders next Sunday. The Czech champions have won a single game out of 23 in the Champions League -- on their debut in the competition against Steaua Bucharest in September 2007. "Of course the longer it gets, the more unpleasant it is," said Jindrich Trpisovsky, the Slavia manager since 2017. Record holders AEK Athens failed to win 24 straight games from 1992-2006, while Steaua, now known as FCSB, recorded 23 winless games between 2006 and 2013. Slavia host Arsenal fresh off the back of their 1-0 victory over Liverpool at Anfield, which would daunt most teams, before Villarreal at home and Bayern Munich away in their next European games. "Of course we know how tough European games are and how hard you must work to win," said Trpisovsky. "In some games we were on the front foot and we got beaten. This is the beauty of football." - 'Unlucky' - Slavia have faced Arsenal three times in the Champions League, recording a draw and two losses including a humiliating 7-0 drubbing in London in 2007. "Slavia simply face the best teams whose quality is obvious," said Vladimir Smicer, a former Slavia striker who won the Champions League with Liverpool in 2005. "I think they were unlucky a few times," he told AFP. item.title: Dak Prescott’s blunt admission puts Brian Schottenheimer under pressure after Cowboys loss
item.description: Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images Dak Prescott has admitted the Dallas Cowboys needed to be more aggressive during their overtime loss to the Arizona Cardinals, adding to the pressure on head coach Brian Schottenheimer after another disappointing offensive performance. Dallas managed just 261 total yards in the defeat while its defence gave up 467. The result leaves the Cowboys at 3-5 and raises further questions about their ability to turn the season around. Prescott completed 19 of 29 passes for 195 yards and a touchdown. He also rushed for 20 yards and another score, but his comments after the game drew attention to the Cowboys’ offensive approach. Dak Prescott wants Brian Schottenheimer to be more aggressive with Dallas Cowboys Speaking to reporters after the loss, Prescott defended Schottenheimer but admitted he would have preferred a different approach against Arizona. “Yeah, I wish we would’ve been more aggressive there.” The quarterback did not directly criticise his head coach, but his admission comes at a difficult time for Schottenheimer. Dallas has struggled offensively in three of its last four games, leaving the coaching staff under increasing scrutiny. Cowboys owner and general manager Jerry Jones was also questioned about Schottenheimer’s position following the defeat. However, Jones insisted the problems extended beyond the head coach. “That’s not in my mind at this time,” Jones said. “This is an indictment of the whole show … This is a criticism of everyone.” Jones also acknowledged that he had previously made a mid-season coaching change, referring to Wade Phillips, but dismissed the possibility of doing the same with Schottenheimer. “I’m not proud of it, but I made a change with Wade Phillips there in the middle of the season,” Jones added. “I don’t see that here at all.” Despite that reassurance, Jones made it clear that the Cowboys’ performances were unacceptable and that responsibility rested with everyone involved. “Well, I don’t know,” Jones said when asked whether he was worried about Schottenheimer. “None of us are getting it done and that should be my concern.” The Cowboys now need to find answers quickly, particularly on offence. Prescott remains central to their hopes of recovering from their poor start, but Schottenheimer’s play-calling will face further scrutiny if Dallas cannot produce a more convincing performance in its next game.
